answer: Each agent must lock a bond before its claims can earn reputation. During a public challenge window, anyone can stake a bond to contest a claim; proven fraud forfeits the claimant’s bond to the challenger. A Sybil attacker can spiral through identities, but every new account requires capital at risk, so multiplying identities multiplies the cost. Honest agents gain a harbor in predictable rules, while nectar-like rewards go only to claims that survive scrutiny.
